note: Inference-time interventions for the model-improvement study. Each method = the FROZEN rev-2 baseline prompt verbatim plus the stated addition (or a decoding change). Developed only on development, discovery and ego-lane fidelity cases; evaluated once on the sealed heldout2 split after freezing.

rgb_scene_context.description: Baseline + scene-context sentence (rendering style is not a depiction cue)
rgb_scene_context.prompt: Classify the marked target in this image. The target is the object inside the yellow rectangle. Allowed labels: physical_vehicle (an actual three-dimensional vehicle present in the scene), flat_depiction (a flat picture or image of a vehicle, for example printed on a board, sign or screen), other (anything else, including flat surfaces or objects that do not show a vehicle), uncertain. Use only visible evidence. If the image does not provide enough information to distinguish a physical vehicle from a depiction, answer uncertain. Return JSON with label and a short visible_evidence string. Do not make driving recommendations. The whole image is a computer rendering of a 3D road scene, so the rendering style itself is not evidence of a depiction: judge whether the marked target is a three-dimensional object standing in that scene or a flat picture placed in it.

rgb_two_step.description: Baseline + two-step decision (vehicle at all? then physical vs picture)
rgb_two_step.prompt: Classify the marked target in this image. The target is the object inside the yellow rectangle. Allowed labels: physical_vehicle (an actual three-dimensional vehicle present in the scene), flat_depiction (a flat picture or image of a vehicle, for example printed on a board, sign or screen), other (anything else, including flat surfaces or objects that do not show a vehicle), uncertain. Use only visible evidence. If the image does not provide enough information to distinguish a physical vehicle from a depiction, answer uncertain. Return JSON with label and a short visible_evidence string. Do not make driving recommendations. Decide in two steps. First: does the marked target show a vehicle at all, either as an object or as an image? If it does not, the label is other. Second, only if it does: is it an actual three-dimensional vehicle in the scene (physical_vehicle) or a flat picture of one (flat_depiction)?
